abertura: You are going to read a group chat from your summer seminar. Before you open it: a chat decides things differently from a conversation.
Mark the three statements that are true of a fast group chat.

itens.t: A decision can be made without anyone writing the word decided.
itens.porque: Yes. Usually somebody proposes, nobody objects, and the group moves on. That silence is the decision.

itens.t: If a date is mentioned, everyone has understood which date it is.
itens.porque: No. In this chat two different days get confused in three messages, and nobody notices.

itens.t: A job that nobody claims usually lands on whoever answers next.
itens.porque: Yes, and naming it out loud is the cheapest way to stop that happening to you.

itens.t: Disagreement in a chat always looks like disagreement.
itens.porque: No. It often looks like a joke, or like one short word, and it still has to be answered.

itens.t: The most useful message is often the one that repeats what was agreed.
itens.porque: Yes. It looks redundant and it is the message everyone scrolls back to find.

itens.t: Reading a chat slowly is the safest way to catch everything.
itens.porque: No. Slow reading catches the words and misses the shape: what was settled, what is open, and by when.

sec1.rationale: A chat is not a conversation with timestamps. Things get settled by silence, jobs get assigned by nobody, and the only person who is safe is the one who says out loud what has just been agreed.

nota.texto: Your reading in English is strong. What this block works on is the part after you understand: saying it back, in your own words, fast enough to be useful to somebody else.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression. You will use all six in class.

I am making the decision on my own

alts: I am complaining about the confusion
I am asking for one of two options, not both
itens.ok: I am asking for one of two options, not both

itens.t: The deadline is X, not Y.
alts: I am correcting a date somebody has mixed up
I am asking when the deadline is
itens.ok: I am correcting a date somebody has mixed up

itens.t: I can take…
alts: I am volunteering for a specific job
I am asking somebody else to do it
itens.ok: I am volunteering for a specific job

itens.t: Can we push X to Y?
alts: I am asking to move something later
I am saying I will not do it
itens.ok: I am asking to move something later

itens.t: One thing nobody has picked up is…
alts: I am naming a job with no owner
I am blaming the group
itens.ok: I am naming a job with no owner

nota.texto: None of them adds information to the chat. Each one does something to what is already there: summarizes it, checks it, corrects it, claims it, moves it, or points at the hole. That is why they work in a group where everyone is talking at once.

abertura: Each line below comes from the chat. What is it doing?

itens.t: “I nominate the Vermeer”
itens.ok: a decision
itens.porque: It starts as a proposal and nobody objects to the work itself, so by the end of the chat it is the decision.

itens.t: “bold choice for a group that has to say something new about it”
itens.ok: a joke
itens.porque: A joke with an argument inside it. He is not against the Vermeer; he is saying it is hard to be original about it.

itens.t: “any chance we push it to Friday”
itens.ok: a request
itens.porque: A request, and it gets refused two lines later. Requests that are refused are the ones people remember as decisions.

itens.t: “she means the check-in call. it’s Thursday 6pm your time”
itens.ok: a correction
itens.porque: A correction of a misunderstanding about which Thursday thing they are talking about.

itens.t: “slides are due Sunday”
itens.ok: a decision
itens.porque: Not up for discussion: it is the fixed point everything else has to fit around.

itens.t: “not it”
itens.ok: a joke
itens.porque: A joke, and the most expensive one in the chat. Two people said it and the email still has no owner.

nota.titulo: The line that costs the most
nota.texto: not it is how English-speaking teenagers refuse a job without refusing it. It is funny, and it leaves the task with whoever speaks last, or whoever cares most. In this chat, that could easily be you.

abertura: Mark the three statements that are true of the chat.

itens.t: The group agreed on the work, even though nobody wrote the word yes.
itens.porque: Yes. Priya proposes, Nate teases, nobody proposes anything else, and the conversation moves on to dates.

itens.t: The check-in call was moved to Friday.
itens.porque: No. Tomas asked, and Priya said they cannot, because the slides are due Sunday.

itens.t: Two different deadlines appear in the chat.
itens.porque: Yes: the check-in call on Thursday and the slides on Sunday. Tomas confused one with the other.

itens.t: Priya is annoyed about doing the slides late.
itens.porque: Yes, and she says it in a way that is easy to scroll past: I am not doing them at 2am again.

itens.t: Somebody has agreed to email the professor.
itens.porque: No. Nate raised it, and both he and Tomas said not it. It has no owner.

itens.t: Nate thinks the Vermeer is a bad choice.
itens.porque: No. He says it is a bold choice because it is hard to say something new, which is an argument about the difficulty, not about the work.

sec4.rationale: One decision, two dates, one job with no owner, and one person who is quietly annoyed. That is the whole shape of the chat, and it fits in four lines when you say it back.

nota.texto: Priya’s 2am line is the only sign that someone is close to being fed up. In class you will not be asked to fix it — only to notice it, because noticing it is what makes the next message you send land well.

nota.texto: Five sentences, and the whole chat fits in them. If you can write it, you can say it — and in class you will say it without the chat in front of you.

opcoes: it is not in the chat

itens.t: The group is presenting the Vermeer.
itens.ok: the group decided it
itens.porque: Decided, by silence: Priya proposed it and nobody put another work on the table.

itens.t: The slides are due on Sunday.
itens.ok: the group decided it
itens.porque: Decided, and it is the fixed point: Priya uses it to refuse the change of day.

itens.t: The check-in call will move to Friday.
itens.ok: somebody suggested it
itens.porque: Suggested by Tomas and refused by Priya in the next line. A request that was answered no.

itens.t: Somebody is emailing Professor Okafor.
itens.ok: it is not in the chat
itens.porque: Not there. Two people said not it, and the job is still sitting in the chat with nobody’s name on it.

itens.t: Priya has done the slides late before.
itens.ok: somebody suggested it
itens.porque: Implied, not stated: I am not doing them at 2am again tells you it has happened, without saying when.

itens.t: Stella is presenting first.
itens.ok: it is not in the chat
itens.porque: Not there at all. Nobody has said anything about the order, which is one more thing the group has not decided.

cl1.prompt: Which of these replies moves the group forward -- and which is just a reaction?

itens.t: “Yeah, the Vermeer works for me, it’s a great painting.”
itens.porque: No. It agrees and adds nothing. After this message the group still does not know who is doing what.

itens.t: “So what we’ve decided is the Vermeer, slides Sunday, call Thursday 6pm. Is that right?”
itens.porque: Yes. It says the decision and both dates back, and it invites a correction if anyone disagrees.

itens.t: “lol not it either”
itens.porque: No. A third not it is funny once and leaves the email exactly where it was.

itens.t: “One thing nobody has picked up is the email. I can take it if someone starts the slides.”
itens.porque: Yes. It names the job with no owner and puts a condition on taking it, in one message.

cl1.rationale: A reaction answers the last message. A move names something the group has not settled -- the decision, a date, or a job -- and gives everyone something to agree with or correct.

callout.titulo: The one that does the most work
callout.texto: So what we’ve decided is… feels redundant when you type it, because everyone was there. It is the message the group scrolls back to find three days later, and the person who wrote it is the person the group trusts with the next decision.

callout.texto: Five is enough for any group message that needs to be read on a phone, between classes. It is also short enough that you will notice which move you skipped. Most people skip the date.
